chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Safwan from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh and Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon them both) said:

«The loan for use (ʿāriyyah) carries no guarantee (ḍamān) on the borrower, except for what is made of gold or silver, for they are guaranteed whether stipulated or not.» And they said: «If a loan for use is borrowed without the owner's permission and it perishes, the borrower is liable.»

key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةُ: Loan for use (borrowing an item for temporary use without compensation)
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: Guarantee/Liability (financial responsibility for loss or damage)
key_terms.مُسْتَعِيرِهَا: The borrower (one who borrows for use)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal liability of a borrower for a borrowed item in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between *ḍamān* (liability) and *ḍarar* (damage) in *ʿāriyyah* contracts, noting that precious metals like gold and silver are inherently guaranteed due to their fungible nature, unlike general goods. The ruling on borrowing without permission (*bi-ghayr idhn*) establishes strict liability, reflecting the principle that unauthorized use voids the presumption of safekeeping. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between accidental loss and negligence in temporary loans.
